name: walkerke/tidycensus
what_it_holds: R package/client wrapping the Census Bureau's Decennial Census and ACS 1-/5-year APIs, returning tidyverse data frames with optional tract/block-group/county geometry (sf). Pulls any ACS table including rental vacancy rate (DP04/B25004), gross rent as % of income / rent burden (B25070/B25071), tenure, and housing-unit counts needed to compute an STR-share-of-housing-stock denominator by tract. 768+ commits, actively maintained, requires free Census API key.
why_useful: This is the standard, well-maintained tool for building the denominator (occupied/vacant housing units, rent burden distribution) that any STR-share-of-housing-stock or rent-burden-vs-STR-density study needs at tract level, nationwide, for any of our 13 Inside Airbnb cities.
size_hint: N/A - library, not a fixed dataset; pulls arbitrary ACS tables on demand
last_activity: active, 768 commits, 22 open issues, 4 open PRs at fetch time
themes: Housing affordability and STR-housing studies data: rent-burden, vacancy, STR share of housing stock by tract
why_all: This is the standard, well-maintained tool for building the denominator (occupied/vacant housing units, rent burden distribution) that any STR-share-of-housing-stock or rent-burden-vs-STR-density study needs at tract level, nationwide, for any of our 13 Inside Airbnb cities.

name: xmunoz/sodapy
what_it_holds: Python client for the Socrata Open Data API. NYC Open Data (data.cityofnewyork.us), LA (data.lacity.org / MyLA311), and San Francisco (datasf.org) all run on Socrata, so this client is the direct mechanism for pulling the NYC 311 Service Requests dataset (Socrata id erm2-nwe9, filterable to complaint types like 'Illegal Vacation Rental Unit', 'Short-Term Rental', 'Illegal Conversion / Illegal Hotel Rental'), LA's MyLA311 service request dataset, and SF 311 Cases, on a point-in-time basis (SoQL supports as_of-style filtering by created_date). No data committed in the repo itself — it is the pull mechanism, not a mirror.
why_useful: Many of the STR housing-stock, rent-burden, and vacancy datasets we still need (municipal housing-court, rent-registry, or vacancy survey tables) live on Socrata portals per city; this is the general-purpose discovery/pull client called out as a gap-#17 method target rather than a one-off scraper.
geography: Global (client works against any Socrata-hosted portal)
themes: Housing affordability and STR-housing studies data: rent-burden, vacancy, STR share of housing stock by tract
Open-data portal discovery: Socrata/CKAN/data.gov/EU data portal clients, dataset search tools, Google Dataset Search scrapers; city portals with STR datasets
Short-term-rental insurance/incident, noise complaint and 311 datasets mentioning Airbnb (NYC 311, LA MyLA311, SF 311) as enforcement/activity proxies
why_all: Many of the STR housing-stock, rent-burden, and vacancy datasets we still need (municipal housing-court, rent-registry, or vacancy survey tables) live on Socrata portals per city; this is the general-purpose discovery/pull client called out as a gap-#17 method target rather than a one-off scraper.

Baseline tooling needed to pull STR registration datasets from any Socrata-hosted city portal named across gaps 8 and 12 (e.g. NYC OSE, Austin licences already held; extend to LA, Toronto-equivalent US cities, lodging-tax collections). Generic — value is in what it's pointed at, not the client itself.

Directly addresses gap #17 (Socrata/CKAN open-data discovery/pull clients) and is the concrete tool to build the exact 311-Airbnb-mention enforcement/activity proxy this theme is scoped around — NYC, LA and SF 311 STR/illegal-hotel complaint volume as a monthly panel, refreshable and point-in-time by created_date.

name: nomadlist (CRAN mirror)

themes: Coliving, corporate housing, furnished mid-term rental data (Blueground, Landing, Furnished Finder, Zeus), remote-work and digital-nomad data (WFH Research SWAA, Nomad List, nomad visas)

name: dbnomics/rdbnomics
what_it_holds: R client (also has Python/other-language siblings) for the DBnomics API (api.db.nomics.world), which aggregates time series from ~90+ national and international statistical providers (Eurostat, IMF, World Bank, ECB, and many national statistical offices/central banks) into one queryable API via rdb(), rdb_datasets(), rdb_providers(). On CRAN and GitHub, 36 stars, 104 commits, mirrored from git.nomics.world. Does not itself contain UK ONS / Banco de Portugal / Norges Bank card-spending series as committed files, but DBnomics as a platform is a single point to check whether those agencies' series (including any card/payment statistics they publish) are mirrored and pullable programmatically.
why_useful: A one-API acquisition method to probe for point-in-time-style pulls of European national-statistics series (potential CHAPS/SIBS/Norges Bank-adjacent series if those agencies publish to DBnomics), relevant to gaps #4 and #6; needs a follow-up check of rdb_providers() output to confirm ONS/BdP/Norges Bank coverage before relying on it.
geography: Global (provider list includes many European national statistical offices/central banks per DBnomics' own description)
size_hint: N/A - API client, not a static dataset
license: Not confirmed on the fetched page (CRAN package; DBnomics platform itself is open data / AGPL-family per its own site, not independently verified here)
last_activity: Active CRAN package; exact last-commit date not shown on fetched page
themes: Public consumer-spend panels: Opportunity Insights Economic Tracker (Affinity card spend), ONS card spending, Bank of England CHAPS, BBVA/CaixaBank research open data, Banco de Portugal SIBS, Norges Bank card data
why_all: A one-API acquisition method to probe for point-in-time-style pulls of European national-statistics series (potential CHAPS/SIBS/Norges Bank-adjacent series if those agencies publish to DBnomics), relevant to gaps #4 and #6; needs a follow-up check of rdb_providers() output to confirm ONS/BdP/Norges Bank coverage before relying on it.

name: nowcast_lstm
what_it_holds: PyTorch LSTM library purpose-built for economic nowcasting (targets growth rates of stationary/seasonally-adjusted series), with automatic hyperparameter tuning/variable selection, uncertainty intervals via synthetic vintage generation, permutation-importance feature contributions, and ARMA-based ragged-edge handling. No datasets committed but ships an example notebook+data zip. 90 commits, MIT, v0.2.6, sibling R/Julia/MATLAB wrappers exist (nowcastLSTM, NowcastLSTM.jl, nowcast_lstm_matlab). Built by a UNCTAD staffer for official nowcasting use.
why_useful: Same use case as FRBNY Nowcasting but a modern, maintained, easier-to-use alternative for mixed-frequency nowcasting of a weekly/quarterly ABNB demand series from assorted alt-data inputs (gap #17).
themes: Real-time and weekly economic indicators: OECD Weekly Tracker (Google Trends based), NY Fed WEI, ONS faster indicators, Dallas Fed mobility, Bundesbank weekly activity index
Nowcasting methods and packages: MIDAS, dynamic factor models, bridge equations, nowcasting with Google Trends, KPI nowcasting for companies
Hotel and STR reviews as demand: review velocity datasets (Google, TripAdvisor, Booking) with dates; review-based nowcasting repos
why_all: Same use case as FRBNY Nowcasting but a modern, maintained, easier-to-use alternative for mixed-frequency nowcasting of a weekly/quarterly ABNB demand series from assorted alt-data inputs (gap #17).

Alternative/competitor method to MIDAS and DFM for the KPI-nowcasting problem in gap #17; benchmarked as best single method in dhopp1/nowcasting_benchmark below — a candidate engine for nowcasting ABNB nights/ADR from ragged alt-data releases (Trends, TSA, calendar-derived indices) ahead of quarter close.

An alt-data-friendly nowcasting engine already designed for irregular/ragged mixed-frequency inputs and synthetic-vintage uncertainty bands -- could take ABNB's weekly calendar-pace/reviews-index/Trends series directly as inputs to nowcast quarterly nights without hand-built bridge equations.

A ready-made mixed-frequency nowcasting method (alternative to MIDAS/DFM) that could ingest a review-velocity series alongside macro series to nowcast nights/ADR -- directly on-theme for gap #17 (nowcasting methods with mixed-frequency data).
